_: Per-incident spec read by incident-overlay.mjs. 'rings' (solid) stay empty until a proof run records a refusal at that badge; only recorded refusals may be ringed. 'dashed' marks places a rule can be added; its labels never claim the point caught the incident.
title: Keep the agent's local settings out of git

steps.text: You approve "Yes, and don't ask again" on a command that carries a secret.
The command, secret included, is saved to .claude/settings.local.json in the project.
git commit takes the file along with the rest of the code.
git push puts it in the repository, public or not.

rings.label: commit: scan-secrets refuses the staged settings file

refusals.sample: git commit, sample a (API key in the right provider format)
refusals.text:
Potential secret detected in this change. Remove credentials and rotate any exposed keys. ...
- .claude/settings.local.json: content pattern

refusals.sample: git commit, sample b (password in a connection string)

footer: The example rules here are from Chock.
alt: The published harness figure with the incident's path drawn in red: you approve a command that carries a secret, the agent loop runs it through the tool gate, the tool saves it to the settings file, and git commit, git push, CI and the main branch carry it on. Cards off the path are dimmed. A solid ring on the commit badge marks the check that refused two test files at commit; dashed rings mark three places a rule could be added.

dashed.label: your own rule could check here: a secret pasted into the prompt, before it reaches the model and the saved transcript
a rule could check here: the proposed command that carries the secret, before it runs
a rule could notice here, before the commit: the settings file now holds a secret (warns; it cannot undo the write)
